Key deals this week: Visa, London Stock Exchange, Tradeweb Markets, Salesforce, and more
data.description:
Here's a list of key deals reported across sectors this week:

Visa Inc. (V) is said to be in advanced discussions to acquire stablecoin infrastructure and custody company Fireblocks for about $2.5 billion.

Qiagen (QGEN) on Thursday said it has agreed on an all-cash public takeover from private equity firm EQT valuing the European molecular testing company at about €10.8 billion.

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEGY) to acquire credit intelligence provider Octus from Permira for $3.535B in cash.

Medical distributor Cencora (COR) on Wednesday announced an agreement to acquire American Oncology Network, valuing the cancer care provider at $2.4B, including debt.

CBRE Group (CBRE) agreed to acquire Onnec Group Ltd., a provider of data center infrastructure services to companies in Europe and Asia Pacific, in a move that will enhance CBRE's ability to support clients' data center needs globally, the company said Tuesday.

Salesforce (CRM) agreed to buy Braze (BRZE), an AI-powered marketing platform, for $5.66B in enterprise value. Braze jumped 51%, while Salesforce fell 1.4%.

Tradeweb Markets (TW) stock jumped 3.7% in Monday after-hours trading after the company announced an agreement to acquire Trumid Holdings, a financial technology company, for $1.97B.

DXC Technology (DXC) is in advanced discussions to sell its insurance software and services unit to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion.

Merck KGaA (MKGAY) (MKGAF) has agreed to acquire Silence Therapeutics (SLN) in an all-cash deal with an enterprise value of $1.1B and an equity value of ~$1.3B.

Silgan Holdings (SLGN) jumped 5.8% pre-market Monday after the packaging solutions company and funds affiliated with American Industrial Partners announced a deal to buy Trivium Packaging in an all-cash deal that values Trivium at ~$3.4B enterprise value.

data.title: Insider trades: Blackberry, Accenture and Cleveland-Cliffs among notable names
data.description:
This week insider transactions were seen across firms like Blackberry, Accenture, Cleveland-Cliffs. The following is the list of deals that took place during the week.

BlackBerry (BB) CEO John Giamatteo sold a combined 250,000 shares of the company’s stock in two transactions on October 21 and 22. On October 21, he sold 151,000 shares at an average price of $9.40 per share, totaling $1,419,400. The following day, he sold an additional 99,000 shares at an average price of $8.74 per share, amounting to $865,260. The two transactions totaled $2,284,660. Following both the sale, Giamatteo directly owned 542, 494 shares. CEO had sold a total of 56726 in earlier October 

Accenture (ACN) CEO Ryoji Sekido sold 5,844 shares at an average price of $244.84, generating approximately $1.43 million and reducing his direct holdings by 83% to 1,194 shares.

Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) Director Edilson Camara purchased 7,400 shares of the company’s stock on Thursday, October 22, at an average price of $13.49 per share, bringing the total transaction value to $99,826. Following the purchase, Camara held 64,717 shares in the company, valued at approximately $873,032.33. The acquisition increased his ownership stake by 12.91%.

Several executives at the Dynex Capital (DX) recently increased their holdings through insider purchases. Co-CEO and President Smriti Laxman Popenoe acquired 10,000 shares of common stock at $10.62 per share, totaling approximately $106,200, along with 2,000 shares of Series D preferred stock at $25.18 per share, valued at $50,360, bringing her total purchase to approximately $156,560. Co-CEO and Chairman Byron L. Boston purchased 9,180 shares of common stock worth approximately $99,970, while CFO Michael Andrew Sartori acquired 1,000 shares at $10.70 per share for a total of $10,700, increasing his direct ownership to 36,579 shares.

PepsiCo (PEP) director Robert C. Pohlad acquired shares around October 14, 2026, including a filing noting 139,571 shares (part of a larger reported acquisition of 184,646 total shares) at a price of $128.28 per share. The total value is approximately $17.90 million for that block (or up to ~$23.7 million for the broader acquisition).

Wes Cummins, CEO and Chairman of Applied Digital (APLD), purchased 55,803 shares of the company’s common stock on October 16, 2026, for approximately $1.01 million at $18.04 per share. The insider purchase comes as APLD trades near its 52-week low of $17.65, following a steep 22% decline over the past week. Meanwhile, company President Jason Gechen Zhang acquired 300,000 shares at an average price of $18.86 per share, representing an investment of approximately $5.66 million.

data.title: Zymeworks early-stage results on ADC show anti-tumor activity in ovarian cancer
data.description:
• Phase 1 data on Zymeworks' (ZYME) ZW191 found that the folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate led to strong anti-tumor activity in ovarian cancer patients that received many prior lines of therapy.
  • In the 6.4 mg/kg dose group, the confirmed objective response rate (cORR) was 64.5% in individuals with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. At the 9.6 mg/kg dose, the figure was 55.3%.
  • cORRs were 69.2% in patients with high FRα expression, 50% in those with intermediate FRα expression, and 55% in individuals with low or negative FRα expression.
  • The disease control rate was, respectively, 100% and 92.1%.
  • In both dosage groups, six-month progression-free survival was 61% in both groups. Median PFS was 7.9 months at 6.4 mg/kg and 9.8 months at 9.6 mg/kg.

Couche-Tard makes bid for Cumberland Farms: report
data.description:
• Canada-based convenience store chain Alimentation Couche-Tard (ATD:CA) has made an offer for the privately held convenience and gas station chain Cumberland Farms valued at between $7.5B and $8B, according to a report in the UK's The Times.
  • Cumberland Farms, which has operations mostly in New England as well as a footprint in Germany, is owned by Cumberland Farms Group, formerly known as EG Group.
  • While there are more than 575 Cumberland Farms branded locations across eight states, the company also owns other banners, including Fastrac, Kwik Shop, Quik Stop, Tom Thumb, and Turkey Hill, bringing the total number of US stores to over 1500. Including Europe, it has more than 6200 sites. 
  • In early July, Cumberland Farms filed with the SEC for a proposed IPO.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 82% firms beat EPS estimates, 79% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Earnings season gathered momentum during the last week, with 76 S&P 500 companies reporting results across key sectors, including Financials, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, and Energy.

The results offered a fresh look at corporate earnings growth and revenue trends across banking, consumer spending, industrial activity, and energy markets.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Of the 76 companies reporting, 62 firms (~82%) exceeded EPS expectations, while 10 fell short and 4 matched estimates. Notably, 60 firms (~79%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 76 companies reporting, 48 firms (63%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 28 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 64 firms (~84%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Tesla (TSLA) — Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 consensus, and revenue of $28.05B edged past estimates despite being flat Y/Y. Free cash flow rebounded to $1.53B, while capital spending reached $4.7B; the company lowered its 2026 capex forecast to $20B from $25B.

Meta Platforms (META) — Revenue jumped 26% Y/Y to $64.6B, beating estimates, while adjusted EPS was $7.40 excluding a $9.89B legal charge. Meta forecast Q4 revenue of $73B–$76B and 2026 capex of $135B–$145B as AI spending remains a central focus.

AT&T (T) — Revenue and adjusted EPS beat expectations, with free cash flow at $5.0B and adjusted EBITDA up 5.4% Y/Y to $12.5B. Postpaid phone additions missed expectations; AT&T raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to around $2.40.

Netflix (NFLX) — EPS of $0.87 beat consensus by $0.05, but revenue of $12.87B narrowly missed estimates despite 12% Y/Y growth. Netflix lowered its 2026 advertising revenue target to $2.7B from about $3B, citing a slower rollout of ad-product capabilities.

GE Aerospace (GE) — Adjusted EPS of $2.25 beat estimates by $0.23, while adjusted revenue of $13.29B topped consensus by $407M. Orders surged 49% to $19B, and GE raised its 2026 outlook, supported by demand for engines and commercial services.

IBM (IBM) — EPS of $2.95 beat the $2.88 consensus, while revenue of $17.1B topped estimates of $16.87B. IBM maintained its 2026 revenue-growth outlook of 4%–5%; software and infrastructure both beat consensus.

Procter & Gamble (PG) — Fiscal Q1 2027 sales rose 4% Y/Y to $23.3B, while core EPS increased 1% to $2.00. P&G maintained its full-year organic sales and core EPS growth outlook but raised its estimated after-tax cost headwind to $1.4B.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) — Q3 sales increased 11% Y/Y to $20.7B, while diluted EPS rose to $7.97 from $6.95. The company raised its 2026 outlook for the second consecutive quarter and reported a record $292B backlog, including $52.5B tied to a multiyear PAC-3 missile interceptor award.

RTX (RTX) — Adjusted EPS of $2.26 beat consensus by $0.48, while revenue of $24.97B topped estimates by about $860M. RTX raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $7.65–$7.75 and free cash flow guidance to $9.0B–$9.2B; its backlog reached a record $340B.

General Motors (GM) — Adjusted EPS of $3.70 beat the $3.57 consensus, while revenue rose 2.9% Y/Y to $50.02B, topping estimates. GM narrowed its 2026 adjusted EBIT outlook to $14.5B–$15.5B and announced a new $20B share-repurchase program.

Earnings season accelerates next week, with mega-cap technology leaders Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG) and Amazon (AMZN) in focus alongside Tesla (TSLA), Netflix (NFLX) and Intel (INTC). Industrial and defense heavyweights Boeing (BA), GE Aerospace (GE) and RTX (RTX) are also due to report, alongside financial firms American Express (AXP) and Blackstone (BX), and energy companies SLB (SLB) and Halliburton (HAL).

data.title: Real estate stocks trade mixed as earnings releases pick pace
data.description:
Real estate stocks traded mixed in a week that saw earnings releases gain momentum.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 0.86% week-over-week to 271.41 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was up 0.97% to $42.57.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index and the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.20% during the course of the week.

Big names that reported their quarterly results this week included CBRE Group (CBRE) (EPS beats, Revenue misses) and Crown Castle (CCI) (FFO beats, Revenue misses).

For next week, major real estate companies scheduled to report include Alexandria Real Estate Equities (ARE), Public Storage (PSA), Welltower (WELL), American Tower (AMT), BXP (BXP), CoStar Group (CSGP), Essex Property Trust (ESS), Extra Space Storage (EXR), Ventas (VTR), Equinix (EQIX), Invitation Homes (INVH), Mid-America Apartment Communities (MAA), VICI Properties (VICI), Kimco Realty (KIM), Digital Realty Trust (DLR), Weyerhaeuser (WY), and Federal Realty Investment Trust (FRT).

Weekly Winners & Gainers

Among largecap stocks, CoStar Group (CSGP) led the weekly gainers, adding 4.98% to close at $33.92. The stock has added ~20% in the past month.

Anton Kharitonov, expert at Traders Union, attributes the stock price rally to technical momentum, but warned that "momentum alone cannot sustain a rally — without news or fundamental backing, pullbacks are likely."

Crown Castle (CCI) was also a notable gainer, adding 4.51% during the week to $85.97.

The stock was trading lower despite third-quarter earnings exceeding consensus and full-year guidance being boosted, as site rental revenue was negatively impacted by a decrease in amortization of prepaid rent and straight-lined revenue.

However, CCI surged after SpaceX was said to be aiming to secure a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the U.S., and was in talks with at least one major cellular infrastructure company to reach that goal.

CBRE Group (CBRE) was the top decliner, retreating 7.35% to $123.30. The real estate services provider missed Q3 earnings estimates. 

First Industrial Realty Trust (FR) (-7.35% W/W to $54.44) led the midcap losers after posting mixed Q3 earnings.

Broadstone Net Lease (BNL) (-4.25% W/W to $17.36) was the next on the list. The stock fell as Agree Realty's (ADC) reduced 2026 investment volume guidance pressured the net lease sector in general.

Curbline Properties (CURB) led the winners, adding 8.82% week-over-week to $28.86. The retail REIT posted Q3 earnings in line with estimates and raised its 2026 operating FFO guidance.

Rithm Capital (RITM) advanced 8.43% to close the week at $9.39 as Q3 earnings topped consensus on net servicing revenue surging.

Brandywine Realty Trust (BDN) (+12.17% W/W to $2.95), Arbor Realty Trust (ABR) (+8.55% W/W to $2.92), Fermi (FRMI) (-19.30% W/W to $2.55), Medical Properties Trust (MPT) (-10.30% W/W to $2.70), and Uniti Group (UNIT) (-9.46% W/W to $5.07) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: Six Flags adding seat belts to roller coasters following Georgia park death
data.description:
• Six Flags Entertainment (FUN) CEO John Reilly on Friday said that seat belts would be added to the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, after a man fell off the ride to his death earlier this month.
  • He added that similar coasters at its other parks would also get the seatbelts. Hypercoasters such as Goliath already have a clamshell lap bar restraint.
  • "We have engaged independent engineers and ride inspection specialists to comprehensively review current safety procedures across our entire portfolio of rides and attractions, across all of our parks," Reilly wrote in his message to guests and passholders.
  • Goliath and eight other coasters at five other Six Flags locations are temporarily closed as the investigation into the Oct. 12 incident continues.

data.title: SA Asks: How can General Motors get back on track?
data.description:
Shares of General Motors (GM) slid significantly this week after the legacy automaker released a weaker-than-expected forecast, fanning concerns about the company's rising costs and product strategy.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Daniel Jones and Bernard Zambonin how they thought GM (GM) could get back on track.  

Daniel Jones: This year has not been particularly pleasant for General Motors (GM) shareholders. The car giant has seen its share price drop significantly at a time when the market is up double digits. Global car production is down about 1%. In the U.S. it is up a surprising 1.4%, but in other parts of the world, it is falling rather rapidly. In China, for instance, it has fallen 5.8%.  

But even though the U.S., which is where GM gets a lot of its value, is doing surprisingly well in the automotive production space, the company is losing ground. It has seen its market share go from 17.3% in the first half of last year to just 16.7% during the same period this year.  

In China, GM's (GM) market share has fallen from 7.2% to 6.8%. And in the Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa combined region, its market share has fallen from 4.7% to 4.2%. Only in South America is the company doing surprisingly well, with market share virtually flat. But that accounts for just a small slice of its overall output. 

A year ago, the company was doing far better. I would say that a lot of its recent pain can be attributed to its decision to scale back drastically on electric vehicles. Citing weakening demand in the final quarter of last year, the company took a $6B charge related to its EV investing plans.  

Some of this scale-back may have made sense. After all, the U.S. government ended the $7,500 EV tax credit in September. But now, with oil prices skyrocketing because of the war against Iran, the decision looks like a bad one.

In a relatively short period of time, the company went from being a marginal player in the EV space to being the second largest in the U.S. In Q3 2024, it had a market share of 9.3%, up from 6.1% a year earlier. By Q3 2025, it had ballooned to 15.2%. The latest data that we have covers the final quarter of last year, and in such a short window of time, it had dropped to 10.8%. Almost certainly, it is lower now.  

At the same time, EV sales are rising in the U.S. The third quarter of this year saw a total output of 262,649 vehicles, 6.1% higher than what we saw for the second quarter.  

There's also the longer-term picture. According to one analysis, by 2030, EV sales in the U.S. will account for up to 38% of new car sales.

Management made a long-term decision based on short-term conditions, and shareholders are now paying the price. Reversing that course of action and remaining committed to it is the best path forward for the business to create value for investors. 

(Daniel Jones runs the SA investment newsletter Crude Value Insights.)

Bernard Zambonin: To me, General Motors (GM) already seems to be on the right track. 

In Q3, for example, adjusted operating income grew 22%, and GMNA margins jumped from 6.2% to 8.7%. GM also projects ~$15B in adjusted operating profit for 2026—around 18% higher than in 2025—while its adjusted free cash flow forecast has been raised from $10B to $12B since the beginning of the year.  

In other words, not only has the thesis not been weakened, but GM itself is more optimistic about its operations.
